theory.overview: Shortest path problems find the minimum cost path between vertices in weighted graphs. Key algorithms: Dijkstra (non-negative weights, greedy), Bellman-Ford (handles negative weights, detects negative cycles), Floyd-Warshall (all-pairs shortest paths), A* (heuristic-guided search). These algorithms are fundamental in navigation, network routing, and optimization. This chapter covers each algorithm, their assumptions, complexities, and applications.

sections.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
sections.content: Finds shortest paths from source to all vertices in graph with non-negative edge weights. Greedy: always process vertex with minimum distance. Uses min-heap for efficiency. Time: $O((V+E) \log V)$ with heap, $O(V^2)$ without. Space: $O(V)$. Cannot handle negative weights (greedy choice may be suboptimal). Used in GPS navigation, network routing.
sections.algorithm: Initialize distances to ∞, source to 0. Min-heap of (dist, vertex). While heap: extract min, relax edges. If new distance < current, update and push to heap.

sections.title: Bellman-Ford Algorithm
sections.content: Finds shortest paths from source, handles negative weights. Detects negative cycles reachable from source. Relax all edges V-1 times (max path length without cycles). If V-th relaxation still improves, negative cycle exists. Time: $O(V \times E)$. Space: $O(V)$. Slower than Dijkstra but more general.
sections.algorithm: Initialize distances to ∞, source to 0. Repeat V-1 times: relax all edges. Check for negative cycle.

sections.title: Floyd-Warshall Algorithm
sections.content: All-pairs shortest paths. Dynamic programming: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]). Try each vertex k as intermediate. Time: $O(V^3)$. Space: $O(V^2)$. Handles negative weights (detects negative cycles on diagonal). Simpler to implement than running Dijkstra V times.
sections.algorithm: Initialize dist matrix. For k in 0..V-1: for i in 0..V-1: for j in 0..V-1: dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]).

sections.title: A* Algorithm
sections.content: Heuristic-guided search for shortest path. Cost function f(n) = g(n) + h(n) where g(n) is actual cost from start, h(n) is heuristic estimate to goal. Uses priority queue sorted by f(n). Optimal if heuristic is admissible (never overestimates) and consistent. Used in pathfinding, games.
sections.algorithm: Priority queue by f(n) = g(n) + h(n). Expand node with minimum f. If goal reached, return path.
sections.heuristic: Must be admissible: h(n) ≤ true cost to goal

sections.title: Algorithm Comparison
sections.content: Dijkstra: non-negative weights, single-source, efficient. Bellman-Ford: negative weights, single-source, slower. Floyd-Warshall: all-pairs, simple, $O(V^3)$. A*: heuristic-guided, single-target, faster with good heuristic. BFS: unweighted, single-source, $O(V+E)$. Choose based on graph properties and requirements.

keyConcepts.name: Relaxation
keyConcepts.description: If dist[u] + weight(u,v) < dist[v], update dist[v] = dist[u] + weight(u,v). Core operation in all shortest path algorithms.

keyConcepts.name: Negative Cycle
keyConcepts.description: Cycle with total weight < 0. Can make shortest paths undefined (can keep going around cycle to decrease distance infinitely). Bellman-Ford detects these.
keyConcepts.detection: After V-1 relaxations, if any edge can still be relaxed, negative cycle exists

keyConcepts.name: Heuristic Admissibility
keyConcepts.description: Heuristic h(n) is admissible if h(n) ≤ true cost to goal. Ensures A* finds optimal path. Consistent heuristic also satisfies triangle inequality.

keyConcepts.name: Greedy Choice
keyConcepts.description: Dijkstra's greedy choice: always process vertex with minimum distance. Works because non-negative weights ensure no better path through unprocessed vertices.

complexity.astar: Depends on heuristic, typically $O(E)$ for good heuristics

steps.title: Dijkstra - Initialize
steps.description: Set all distances to ∞ except source (0). Add source to min-heap.

steps.title: Extract Minimum
steps.description: Extract vertex with minimum distance from heap. If already processed, skip.
steps.code: d, u = heappop(heap); if d > dist[u]: continue;

steps.title: Relax Edges
steps.description: For each neighbor v: if dist[u] + w(u,v) < dist[v], update dist[v] and push to heap.
steps.code: for v, w in neighbors[u]: if dist[u] + w < dist[v]: dist[v] = dist[u] + w; heappush(heap, (dist[v], v));

steps.title: Repeat
steps.description: Continue until heap empty. All shortest distances computed.

steps.title: Reconstruct Path
steps.description: Track predecessor during relaxation. Reconstruct path by backtracking from target.
steps.code: path = []; while target != source: path.append(target); target = pred[target]; path.append(source); return path[::-1];

practiceProblems.title: Network Delay Time
practiceProblems.description: Find time for signal to reach all nodes (max shortest path from source).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra from source K. Return max distance or -1 if any unreachable.

practiceProblems.title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
practiceProblems.description: Find cheapest flight from src to dst with at most K stops.
practiceProblems.solution: Bellman-Ford variant. Relax edges K+1 times (K stops = K+1 edges). Track min cost.

practiceProblems.title: Path with Minimum Effort
practiceProblems.description: Find path minimizing maximum height difference (edge weight = abs diff).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra variant: min-heap by max effort. Track minimum max effort to each cell.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path from top-left to bottom-right (8 directions, can only pass through 0).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS (unweighted). Queue stores (row, col, distance).

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path removing at most k obstacles.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS on state (row, col, removed). Track visited states.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Cost to Reach City
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum cost to reach destination with discounts (can use at most one discount).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra with state (node, used_discount). Two copies of each node.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path visiting all nodes in undirected graph.
practiceProblems.solution: BFS on state (node, visited_mask). State space = node × all visited subsets.

practiceProblems.title: Dijkstra with Early Stop
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path to specific target (can stop early).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra, stop when target extracted from heap.

practiceProblems.title: Reconstruct Itinerary
practiceProblems.description: Reconstruct itinerary in lexical order given tickets (Eulerian path).
practiceProblems.solution: Hierholzer's algorithm. DFS, remove edges, add to result in reverse.

practiceProblems.title: Floyd-Warshall Implementation
practiceProblems.description: Implement Floyd-Warshall to find all-pairs shortest paths.
practiceProblems.solution: Initialize dist matrix. Triple nested loops: k, i, j. dist[i][j] = min(dist[i][j], dist[i][k] + dist[k][j]).
practiceProblems.hints: Triple nested loops, k in outermost

practiceProblems.title: Detect Negative Cycle
practiceProblems.description: Detect negative cycle in weighted directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Bellman-Ford. After V-1 relaxations, if any edge can still be relaxed, negative cycle exists.

practiceProblems.title: Currency Arbitrage
practiceProblems.description: Detect arbitrage opportunity (cycle with product > 1).
practiceProblems.solution: Bellman-Ford on -log(weights). Negative cycle = arbitrage.

practiceProblems.title: A* Pathfinding
practiceProblems.description: Implement A* for grid pathfinding with Manhattan distance heuristic.
practiceProblems.solution: Priority queue by f = g + h. g = actual cost, h = Manhattan distance to goal.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Spanning Tree
practiceProblems.description: Find MST using Prim's or Kruskal's algorithm.
practiceProblems.solution: Prim's: start from any vertex, add min edge to cut. Kruskal's: sort edges, add if connects different components (Union-Find).

practiceProblems.title: Second Minimum Time to Reach Destination
practiceProblems.description: Find second shortest path from source to destination.
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra with two distances per node (best, second best). Update both when relaxing.
practiceProblems.hints: Dijkstra with two distances per node

practiceProblems.title: Constrained Shortest Path
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest path with constraint (e.g., must visit certain nodes).
practiceProblems.solution: State-space Dijkstra. State includes visited required nodes.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Path in Directed Acyclic Graph
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest paths in DAG (can be done in O(V+E)).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort, then relax edges in topological order.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Path in DAG
practiceProblems.description: Find longest path in DAG (can be done in O(V+E)).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort, negate weights, find shortest path, or DP with topological order.

practiceProblems.title: Critical Path Method
practiceProblems.description: Find longest path in DAG (project scheduling).
practiceProblems.solution: Topological sort, DP to find longest path to each node.
practiceProblems.hints: Topological sort, DP for longest path

practiceProblems.title: Word Ladder
practiceProblems.description: Find shortest transformation sequence (BFS = shortest path in unweighted graph).
practiceProblems.solution: BFS from beginWord. Each edge = one letter change.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Number of Vertices to Reach All Nodes
practiceProblems.description: Find minimum vertices to reach all nodes in directed graph.
practiceProblems.solution: Find strongly connected components (Kosaraju or Tarjan). Count components with no incoming edges.
practiceProblems.hints: SCC, count components with no incoming edges

practiceProblems.title: Find the City With Smallest Neighbors
practiceProblems.description: Find city with smallest number of neighbors at distance threshold.
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra from each city, count reachable within threshold.

practiceProblems.title: Minimum Score Path
practiceProblems.description: Find path minimizing maximum edge weight (minimax path).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra variant: min-heap by max edge weight on path.
practiceProblems.hints: Dijkstra, min-heap by max edge weight

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Probability Path
practiceProblems.description: Find path maximizing product of probabilities (multiply instead of add).
practiceProblems.solution: Dijkstra with multiplication. Use -log to convert to addition, or use max-heap.

practiceProblems.title: Shortest Distance After Road Additions
practiceProblems.description: Answer queries about shortest path after adding roads.
practiceProblems.solution: Floyd-Warshall after each addition, or incremental updates.
